verdict: Corpay grew revenue 18% to $1,382M as Corporate Payments jumped 41%, and profit attributable to Corpay rose 36% to $378M.

kpis.label: Revenue
kpis.note: +18% vs a year ago — 11% organic growth (ignoring deals and currency)

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: vs $3.91 a year ago — attributable to Corpay; consolidated net income was $382M

kpis.label: Adjusted EPS (non-GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: +32% YoY — excludes stock pay, amortization and deal costs

kpis.label: Corporate Payments revenue
kpis.note: +41% YoY — helped by the Alpha acquisition, closed in late 2025

segments.name: Corporate Payments
segments.note: Cards and software that help companies control spending and pay bills, plus cross-border payments (paying suppliers in other currencies). Up 41%, helped by the Alpha acquisition; organic growth was 18%.

segments.name: Vehicle Payments
segments.note: Fuel cards and payment tools for vehicle fleets — the biggest business this quarter. Up 8%.

segments.name: Lodging Payments
segments.note: Paying for hotel rooms for travelling work crews. Up 3%.

segments.name: Other
segments.note: Gift cards, outsourced card processing and payroll cards. Down 2%.

opex.name: Selling
opex.note: Sales teams and commissions. Up 24% YoY as the company grew.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: Running the company — finance, legal, technology and admin. As reported it was $204M; it is shown here at $202M, net of a $3M gain on disposition and other operating costs that round to $0M, plus a $1M rounding adjustment so the lines tie — see the footer note.

opex.name: Depreciation and amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of equipment, software and bought intangible assets over their useful lives. Up 24% YoY, partly because of acquisitions.

otherDetail: Other expense was $119M, net: $109M of interest expense, net, plus $10M of other expense, net.

takeaways.title: Growth was broad, led by corporate payments
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 18% to $1,382M. Corporate Payments jumped 41% to $571M (18% without the Alpha deal), Vehicle Payments rose 8% to $580M and Lodging rose 3% to $131M. Management raised full-year revenue guidance to about $5.35B.

takeaways.title: Very high margins held up
takeaways.text: Adjusted EBITDA (a cash-profit measure that leaves out interest, tax, depreciation and one-offs) was $794M, up 17%, for a 57.4% margin — almost unchanged from 57.7% a year ago. On a GAAP basis, operating profit was $621M, a 45% margin.

takeaways.title: Profit rose faster than revenue
takeaways.text: Net income attributable to Corpay rose 36% to $378M, and EPS rose 45% to $5.66, helped by buybacks: Corpay repurchased 1.9M shares for $747M in the quarter alone, so each remaining share claims a bigger slice of profit.

oneTimers: Integration and deal-related costs were $17M in the quarter and restructuring costs were $6M. Corpay excludes both from its adjusted results — a big part of why adjusted EPS ($7.54) sits well above GAAP EPS ($5.66).

Corpay booked a $3M gain on disposition (selling a business or asset) in the quarter; in the flow above it is netted into general and administrative costs. Its adjusted results also add back a $19M adjustment at an equity-method investment (a minority stake whose results Corpay shares in).
footerNote: Corpay reports no gross-profit line: processing expenses are treated here as the cost of revenue. Figures are rounded to $M.
follow100Note: The flow uses consolidated net income of $382M; $4M was attributable to noncontrolling interests, leaving $378M attributable to Corpay.
